### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/data/authoring-key-lint.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**22** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 93fa9118a3dc61473890eafc6bb170a6fc1c3042`.

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/data/authoring-key-lint.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 93fa9118a3dc61473890eafc6bb170a6fc1c3042` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3d5545b44da7442ae521fb381accdfe522065287` — the merge of head `9978932c43b335aeb436b65bbdc025dcb8f6a31e` into base `93fa9118a3dc61473890eafc6bb170a6fc1c3042`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3d5545b44da7442ae521fb381accdfe522065287 && git checkout 3d5545b44da7442ae521fb381accdfe522065287
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 93fa9118a3dc61473890eafc6bb170a6fc1c3042 9978932c43b335aeb436b65bbdc025dcb8f6a31e && git checkout -B drift-repro 93fa9118a3dc61473890eafc6bb170a6fc1c3042 && git merge --no-ff 9978932c43b335aeb436b65bbdc025dcb8f6a31e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 93fa9118a3dc61473890eafc6bb170a6fc1c3042
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 93fa9118a3dc61473890eafc6bb170a6fc1c3042` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `396a54f9f1b15f1986f27add831de9e47284404d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/authoring-key-lint.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts + none

Inputs read: card #36776 with its three comments (triage 7114582275, claim 7230446042, os-dev report 7231083102), the PR body and its three comments, the net diff against `27ee98438e61148e581b710e828bc51639361ff1` (5 files, +119 −10), and the 69 check-runs on the head (58 success, 11 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending). Code outside the diff was read at the head, not reviewed: `field-history-default.ts`, `masked-field-types.ts`, `field.zod.ts`, `field-key-aliases.ts`, `plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts`, `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx`, `ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/FieldHistory.tsx`.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set: unchanged — right. The diff changes four string values (`CAPABILITIES_RETIRED_KEY_GUIDANCE.trash`, `UNKNOWN_KEY_GUIDANCE.versioning`, `FIELD_KEY_GUIDANCE.audit.why`, `FIELD_KEY_GUIDANCE.auditTrail.why`), adds one module-private string constant, and edits one TSDoc. No key is added to or removed from a guidance map, no `to` or `why` changes kind (so no row moves between alias and guidance in `fieldKeyGuidanceAsStrictOptions`), and no schema shape, `.describe()` or export changes. "Every key that was refused is still refused, and nothing is newly refused" holds.
- Module-init order: right. `FIELD_HISTORY_PRESCRIPTION` is declared above `CAPABILITIES_RETIRED_KEY_GUIDANCE` and far above `UNKNOWN_KEY_GUIDANCE`, so the eager-construction order the `ObjectCapabilities` docblock warns about is kept.
- Public surface: the constant is not exported, so `api-surface` and `export-origins` do not move; `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Spec property liveness`, `Type Check · workspace` and `Test Core` are success on the head.
- Published text: the four refusal messages change. No other copy of the old sentences exists in the head tree outside `CHANGELOG.md` history.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` patch with `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, on both the PR body and the changeset — right. What an author can write is unchanged, and no meaning or default moves; only the prescription text does. `Check Changeset` is success.

Changeset prose, sentence by sentence against the tree: the account of field `trackHistory` (opts in a media or structured-JSON type, `false` turns nothing off) matches `resolveFieldHistory`; `enable.trackHistory` opens the ledger and not the values (`RecordDetailView` `historyEnabled` reads `sys_audit_log` only on `trackHistory === true`, while the activity stream is gated on `enable.activities` alone); "wording only" and "nothing to migrate" hold. The one sentence that inherits S1 is "field history needs no key".

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty. `security_findings`: none.
- Out-of-scope flag, `skills/objectstack-project/evals/project-process.json:145` ("sets `trackHistory` where field-level history is wanted"): confirmed at the head, correctly left out (governed `skills/**`, outside the card). Follow-up card for the seat.
- Deviation (push hook refused a `Refs` line, amended before first push): no effect on the head.
- Two gates the dev left unmeasured locally (`check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`): answered by the head's green `Lint & Repo Gates` and `Build Core`.
- SQL push-down: no query, id materialisation or join in the diff.
- Further follow-ups outside the card's `packages/spec` scope, none a finding here: `content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx:1063` (field `trackHistory` described as the timeline switch), `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx:81,94`, `content/docs/data-modeling/schema-design.mdx:68`, `content/docs/protocol/objectql/schema.mdx:239` and `content/docs/protocol/objectql/index.mdx:89` (object `trackHistory` glossed as "field history tracking"), and the comment "object/field `trackHistory`" in `packages/spec/src/system/index.ts:45` and `security-context.zod.ts:17` (the latter is rendered into `content/docs/references/system/security-context.mdx:16`).

### ④ Design judgment

Read against `resolveFieldHistory`, the writer (`changeValuesShownFor` and `renderTrackedChangeSummary` in `audit-writers.ts`) and the readers.

True as written:
- `enable.fieldHistory: false` is the object's off switch (first line of `resolveFieldHistory`; it wins over any field flag).
- A field's own `fieldHistory: false` is an opt-out.
- `fieldHistory: true` opts a default-off type in. The spec's own idiom "media or structured-JSON" stands for the 14 types of `FIELD_HISTORY_DEFAULT_OFF_TYPES` (image, file, avatar, video, audio, signature, composite, repeater, record, location, address, code, json, vector).
- Field `trackHistory: false` turns nothing off, and `true` matters only for those types; object `trackHistory` gates the ledger view and the `history` verb, not the values.
- The values show on the record activity timeline without `enable.trackHistory`: the stream is read on `enable.activities !== false` alone.
- The `activityMilestones` TSDoc now agrees with the code.

Findings:

S1 (should-fix) — `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`, `FIELD_HISTORY_PRESCRIPTION`: "Field history needs no key: a changed field's old → new values show … by default" is false for the 14 default-off types. `resolveFieldHistory({ type: 'json' }, {})` is `false`; such a field shows values only with `fieldHistory: true`. The `audit` / `auditTrail` rows in this same PR carry the exception in a parenthesis, and so do `Field.fieldHistory`'s `.describe()` and the `tracked` guidance; the shared constant used by `enable.trash` and `versioning` does not. For exactly these types the old text (use per-field `trackHistory`) did turn values on, so the new sentence is a step back for them. Fix: add the same parenthesis to the constant and pin it. Note for the seat: the sentence matches the card's done-when wording and `enable.fieldHistory`'s own `.describe()`, so it is not a must-fix.

S2 (should-fix) — card done-when 2 is not met, while the PR says `Fixes #36776` and the claim's re-check says no string in `packages/spec/src` still sends authors to per-field `trackHistory`. `packages/spec/src/data/field-key-aliases.ts:95` keeps `trackChanges: 'trackHistory', feedTracked: 'trackHistory'` in `FieldSchema`'s alias table, so a field written with `trackChanges: false` is refused with a rename to `trackHistory`, the flag whose `false` turns nothing off. The neighbouring `tracked` key is already answered in prose with the `fieldHistory` model. The file is outside the claim's file surface, so this closes one of two ways: fix it here (the two rows become prose guidance like `tracked`; both keys stay refused), or the seat files a follow-up card and the PR body states that done-when 2 is left open for these two rows. The second way does not move the head.

Nits (no effect on the contract, accepted as deviations or a follow-up):
- N1 — the sentences omit conditions that also keep values off: `enable.activities: false` (no activity row is written at all), a credential field (`secret`, and `password` outside a `better-auth` object), and the computed types (`formula`, `summary`, `rollup`, `autonumber`), whose changes the writer never diffs. `Field.fieldHistory`'s `.describe()` names the credential case; a refusal need not.
- N2 — the pin "the prescription agrees with resolveFieldHistory" cross-checks four of the claims in code, but not the `fieldHistory: true` opt-in for a media type that the `audit` rows state; that sentence is pinned as text only.

Pins: each new refusal sentence is pinned and goes red on the old text, by reading. `enable.trash` and `versioning`: the default sentence, both off switches, the retention half (the regex needs the new "For retention, " form) and the absence of `trackHistory`; the 16.0 tombstone table needle moved to `fieldHistory`. `audit` and `auditTrail`: three sentences and the absence of `trackHistory`, through `FieldSchema.safeParse`. This agrees with the dev's ablation counts (2, 3, 2, 2). `Test Core` is success on the head.

No must-fix. S1 and S2 are open on this head.

Inputs — these and nothing else:
  · card #36776: its body and EVERY comment (rulings and earlier records included)
  · PR #38064: its body, its file list, and the net diff against `main` at `27ee98438e61148e581b710e828bc51639361ff1`
  · the check-runs on `396a54f9f1b15f1986f27add831de9e47284404d`: their conclusions ARE the gate verdicts
⛔ Not the dispatch order, ⛔ not the dispatching seat's own conclusions — this brief is adversarial by design.

Scope — the paths `reviewFace` returns as `hits` on this PR's file list: packages/spec/src/data/authoring-key-lint.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts;
  plus every file IN THIS DIFF that directly implements or enforces them — the gate that enforces a rule, the code
  a jsdoc or schema line describes, the validator a skill teaches — reviewed for agreement with the contract.
  Widen it freely, ⛔ never below `hits`; the record's `Scope:` line names the implementing files apart from `hits`.
  The rest of the diff (tests, unrelated modules, lockfiles, generated output, changesets) is the lane seat's
  ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, exactly as a standalone PR of those files.
  ④ judges the `hits` files and those implementing files ONLY:
  lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in the PR are not reviewed;
  code outside the diff is READ to judge them, never reviewed.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/166e2125-4268-552f-a555-2b7c43a99f0f/scratchpad/pr-38064/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
     On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
     finding unless a reason is given (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first).
  ④ Design judgment — for EVERY `hits` file: does the change hold against the code it cites and the
     scenario it is accepted against? A skill file against the card's eval prompt and the spec it teaches
     on `main`; a schema file against the ruling or ADR it implements and its first consumer; an ADR
     against its first consumer and its execution plan. For EVERY implementing file in the diff: does the
     code agree with the contract, sentence by sentence? Read the cited code in the live tree, and try to
     break the design.
     Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
     A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
     Spell a must-fix or should-fix with its id and grade, `S1 (should-fix) — …`, and a clean round as
     `No must-fix, no should-fix.`: the queue guard reads a graded finding as OPEN on this head and
     refuses the record; the delta record names those it closes by id alone, `S1: closed`.
     A nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card: a fix
     anywhere else moves the head, and this record no longer covers it.
     ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.
Sign `Implemented-by:` with the dev's branch and `Reviewed-by:` with your session id — the value is the FIRST
thing after each colon.

**L1 REWORK** at `396a54f9f1b15f1986f27add831de9e47284404d` (L1-a for the seat). The published-schema face (`object.zod.ts`, `authoring-key-lint.ts`) owes an L2. The isolated `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` record 7231559159 is a **PASS** (claim 7231496616, filled brief 7231565437, `verify-review-tier` PASS). It has no must-fix, but it has two **should-fix** findings, and each owes a delta.

**What holds.**
- **Wording only.** Four string values, one unexported constant and one TSDoc change. Every key refused before is still refused, and nothing new is refused.
- **Declarations.** `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none` and the patch level are right.
- **The model matches the code.** `enable.fieldHistory: false` is the object's off switch. A field's `fieldHistory: false` opts it out. `fieldHistory: true` opts a default-off type in. A field's `trackHistory: false` turns nothing off, and the object's `trackHistory` gates only the ledger view.
- **Pins.** Each new refusal sentence has a pin that goes red on the old text. CI is 58 success, 11 expected skip, 0 failed.

**Owed before ACCEPT.**
- **S1 (should-fix): the shared `FIELD_HISTORY_PRESCRIPTION` overstates the default.** "Field history needs no key: … values show … by default" is false for the 14 default-off types: image, file, avatar, video, audio, signature, composite, repeater, record, location, address, code, json, vector. `resolveFieldHistory({ type: 'json' }, {})` returns `false`. The `audit` / `auditTrail` rows carry the exception in a parenthesis, but the `enable.trash` / `versioning` sentence does not. For those types the old advice did turn values on, so the new text is a step back there. **Fix:** add the same exception (`fieldHistory: true` opts a media or structured-JSON field in) to the shared constant, with a pin. The changeset's "field history needs no key" inherits this, so fix both in one push.
- **S2 (should-fix): card done-when 2 is not met, yet the PR says `Fixes #36776`.** In `packages/spec/src/data/field-key-aliases.ts`, `FieldSchema`'s alias table still has `trackChanges: 'trackHistory'` and `feedTracked: 'trackHistory'`. So `trackChanges: false` is refused with a rename to the flag whose `false` turns nothing off. Close it one of two ways:
  - **(a)** fix those two rows here. The neighbouring `tracked` key is already answered in prose, which is the precedent.
  - **(b)** file a follow-up card, make the first line `Part of #36776`, and add a body note that done-when 2 stays open for these two rows.

  (a) moves the head together with S1. (b) is a body edit only.

**Nits (not blocking).**
- N1: the sentences leave out the other conditions that keep values off: `enable.activities: false` (no row is written), credential fields (`secret`, and `password` outside a `better-auth` object), and computed types (formula, summary, rollup, autonumber), which the writer never diffs.
- N2: the `resolveFieldHistory` cross-check does not cover the `fieldHistory: true` opt-in, which is pinned as text only.

- `skills/objectstack-project/evals/project-process.json:145`
- `content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx:1063`, `objects.mdx:81,94`, `schema-design.mdx:68`
